  Expected change site: .github/workflows/orchestrate.yml, "Pre-assemble static context" step, lines 578-589.
  Evidence of absence: The last run added render-with-fallback to all four static-context readers. Three of them -- orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, and scripts/validate_process.sh -- select AGENTS.md first then agents.md before the render call, correctly covering consumer repos that use AGENTS.md casing. The orchestrator assembler at orchestrate.yml lines 578-589 still hard-codes [ -f agents.md ] in the outer if-guard and passes --agents-file agents.md to the assembler. When a consumer repo uses AGENTS.md (the common consumer casing), [ -f agents.md ] is false, the elif symlink-guard also fails, and no agents section reaches the orchestrator prompt at all. Pending agents.d/ fragments are invisible to the orchestrator in those repos. The other three readers in the same change set were given casing selection; this one was left with the lower-case-only path it had before the last run.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: PR description and README contract paragraph state "Readers see pending fragments: scripts/build_static_context.sh and the orchestrate, clarify-respond, poller-judge and validate static-context assemblers render them into the model's agents context (falling back to the plain file)". The LAST RUN delivered render-with-fallback for the orchestrate reader, but the implementation is incomplete compared to the other three readers it was meant to match.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/orchestrate.yml, "Pre-assemble static context" step, lines 577-588.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN's new block still gates only on lowercase agents.md:

```
if [ -f agents.md ] && [ ! -L agents.md ]; then
  echo "=== AGENTS.MD ==="
  if [ -d agents.d ] && [ ! -L agents.d ] && orchestrate_agents_render="$(PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -I -B scripts/assemble_agents.py render --repo-root . --agents-file agents.md 2>/dev/null)"; then
    printf '%s\n' "${orchestrate_agents_render}"
  else
    cat agents.md
  fi
  echo
elif [ -L agents.md ]; then
  echo "::warning::agents.md is a symbolic link; omitted from the static context." >&2
fi
```

The other three readers modified or referenced in the same LAST RUN (orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml lines 736-755, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 1409-1428, scripts/validate_process.sh lines 3077-3096) all set a `*_agents_file` variable by picking `AGENTS.md` first, then `agents.md`, before the render-with-fallback block. orchestrate.yml is the only one of the four that hard-codes lowercase `agents.md` in both the outer if-check and the `--agents-file` argument. The elif "[ -L agents.md ]" branch fires only when agents.md exists as a symlink; when the agents file is named `AGENTS.md` (no agents.md at all), neither the if nor the elif matches, and the orchestrator prompt is silently emitted with no agents section. The previous editor round acknowledged this in the editor's own log (comment 6097187202: "Effect until it is decided: in a consumer repo whose agents file is named `AGENTS.md`, the orchestrator prompt still gets no agents section at all, so pending fragments are missing too. That is unchanged from before this PR.") and explicitly chose not to fix it, citing a "separate behaviour change" and the "oscillation guard". That deferral is in an editor comment, not in the issue or the PR description, and the README's contract paragraph in the same PR claims orchestrate is a reader. The fix mirrors the three-sibling pattern: pick `AGENTS.md` first, then `agents.md`, then the same render-with-fallback.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- Requirement: The PR's README contract paragraph must accurately describe the readers it claims, so consumer repos and contributors can rely on it. The LAST RUN updated the paragraph to list five readers; the list claims behavior that one of the listed readers (and a pre-existing sibling) does not deliver.
  Expected change site: README.md, "agents.md fragment contract" paragraph (lines 1188-1219) and scripts/build_static_context.sh::emit_agents_md (call sites of `_static_context_cat_agents` at lines 123 and 131).
  Evidence of absence: The README states "scripts/build_static_context.sh and the orchestrate, clarify-respond, poller-judge and validate static-context assemblers render them into the model's agents context". Both scripts/build_static_context.sh and the LAST RUN's orchestrate.yml only invoke `_static_context_cat_agents` / the render branch when the lowercase file `agents.md` exists; neither reads `AGENTS.md` first. The previous editor rounds deferred the build_static_context.sh gap (comments 6096155106 and 6097187202) as a "separate behaviour change" because adding `AGENTS.md` would change the clarify / plan / implement prompts in every consumer repo. That is a real change with consumer-repo prompt implications, but the README in the same PR names the script as a reader; a consumer repo that uses `AGENTS.md` will see a misleading "rendered" claim in the README while the actual render does not happen. Until either the reader is fixed or the README stops naming it, the contract paragraph is inaccurate.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
